content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge is resolving the D5 vs C5 collision over Isaiah 7:14, so it is doing the chain-against-chain assessment the rule governs.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "never verse by verse -- (1) any mention of word-count is a forbidden verse-by-verse test; (2) a word-count noted only as inconclusive does not decide, and the judge may weigh the chains by concession.", "why": "The judge text acknowledges the chapter-bounds chain, notes C5's own narrowing concession, and treats the word-count as non-decisive, so it does not use a stating-verse test and weighs the collision by footing rather than a single verse."}
